title: Word count as map, shuffle and reduce
instructions:
## Why MapReduce can run on a thousand machines

Each phase works on its own slice of data without talking to the others. Write the three phases for the classic word count.

1. `map_line(line)`: a list of `(word, 1)` pairs for the lower-cased words of one line (split on whitespace, strip punctuation `.,!?;:` from both ends).
2. `shuffle(pairs)`: group the pairs by key into a dict `word -> list of counts`.
3. `reduce_counts(word, counts)`: return `(word, total)`.
4. `word_count(lines)`: run map on every line, shuffle, reduce every group, and return a dict `word -> count`.
hints: [(w.strip(".,!?;:").lower(), 1) for w in line.split() if w.strip(".,!?;:")]
The dict comprehension {w: reduce_counts(w, c)[1] for w, c in shuffle(pairs).items()} is the reduce phase.
realityNote: Hadoop ran map tasks where the data blocks lived and shipped only the shuffled pairs over the network; Spark keeps the same shape with map, groupByKey and reduceByKey but holds intermediate data in memory.
